summary: PulseGuard v0.6.26 adds a guarded automatic repair lane for genuine Windows Software Protection (sppsvc.exe) failures without taking ownership of protected folders or blindly replacing Windows service permissions.

sections.heading: Guarded sppsvc automatic repair
sections.detail: When current sppsvc.exe crash evidence exists, FIX + OPTIMIZE ALL now verifies the Microsoft-signed C:\Windows\System32\sppsvc.exe and the registered sppsvc service, verifies Task Scheduler, and first attempts a normal Software Protection service restart. If the service is already running or starts normally, PulseGuard stops there and records the issue as fixed/monitoring.

sections.heading: Access Denied gets a targeted permission check
sections.detail: Only when the service-start result proves Access Denied does PulseGuard inspect C:\Windows\System32\Tasks\Microsoft\Windows\SoftwareProtectionPlatform. It preserves the existing ACL and ownership and adds only missing NETWORK SERVICE Read/Execute access. PulseGuard does not take ownership of the folder.

sections.heading: DISM/SFC and SYSTEM are fallbacks, not the first move
sections.detail: If sppsvc still will not start, PulseGuard runs DISM /RestoreHealth and SFC /scannow and retries. If Access Denied still persists while elevated, PulseGuard creates a temporary Task Scheduler job running as LocalSystem for only the targeted task-folder ACL/service-start operation, waits for the result, and deletes the task/helper immediately afterward.

sections.heading: No blind service security-descriptor replacement
sections.detail: Before privileged fallback, PulseGuard captures sc.exe qc sppsvc and sc.exe sdshow sppsvc evidence. v0.6.26 does not hard-code or replace the sppsvc service SDDL because PulseGuard does not yet bundle a validated Windows-build-specific known-good descriptor. The original descriptor is retained in the report for diagnosis.

sections.heading: Repair verification and historical-event handling
sections.detail: A successful repair requires sppsvc to reach SERVICE_RUNNING. PulseGuard then writes a verified-fix watermark so retained Event Viewer crashes remain available as history but do not reduce the current health score unless a newer crash occurs after the repair.

sections.heading: Detailed repair audit
sections.detail: The consolidated report now includes a SoftwareProtectionRepair section with the trigger crash time, service state before/after, task-folder permission state before/after, whether DISM/SFC or the temporary SYSTEM fallback was used, the original service SDDL, and every repair action taken.
